Undated candidate topics for the blog queue. Nothing here is scheduled. The queue scheduler locks a candidate into a Wed/Sat slot ~14 days before publish, filtered by eligibility window and cannibalization distance, and only if approved. Replaces the practice of dating a year of content up front — see plans/ blog content queue redesign (2026-08-04).

CANDIDATE SHAPE. Required: slug, title, primary_keyword, status, source. The scheduler's candidateToPost() also reads description, topic_type, search_intent, funnel_stage, conversion_goal, related_cluster, page_role and refresh_cycle - it defaults each one, so a candidate missing them still schedules but publishes with generic metadata. check-data-integrity.js warns on those so a hollow entry is visible before it occupies a slot. seasonality_window must be a name from content-taxonomy.json (lifecycle.seasonal.seasonality_windows) or null; anything else is INELIGIBLE ON EVERY DATE since the filter started failing closed, so the build errors on an unknown value rather than letting it sit unschedulable. research_brief carries the researcher's SERP evidence, differentiation angle, direct-answer target, questions, entities and sources; candidateToPost passes it to the dated post, blog-planner injects it into the blog-write task, and seo-auditor's draft gate verifies the draft against it.

candidates.title: Insurance for Plumbing Contractors in Kentucky: A Complete 2026 Guide
candidates.description: A Kentucky-specific guide covering every coverage type plumbing contractors need to license, bid jobs, and protect against water damage claims, with the actual state minimums from DHBC regulations.

research_brief.demand_evidence: The agency already has a plumbing contractors industry page (/industries/plumbing-contractors.html) and the published HVAC and roofing contractor insurance guides have performed well as a cluster. The plumbing guide is the missing sibling. Live SERP shows ContractorNerd, MoneyGeek, and allenthomasgroup.com rank for 'plumbing contractor insurance Kentucky', while rbisomerset.com (a Kentucky independent agency in Somerset) has a targeted post. The agency's existing product page and industry page give it entity authority to rank for a dedicated blog post targeting this query family.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is mixed: ContractorNerd (national, data-heavy, cost-focused), MoneyGeek (aggregator), allenthomasgroup.com (out-of-state independent agency with a Kentucky-specific page), rbisomerset.com (Kentucky independent agency, thin post), and ServiceTitan (trade software). No post combines the Kentucky DHBC licensing insurance minimums (the $250,000 GL minimum from 815 KAR 20:080 for master plumbers), completed operations coverage detail, water damage liability, and a working Kentucky agent's perspective. The allenthomasgroup page is the strongest competitor but is a generic agency not located in Bullitt or Daviess County.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: A post grounded in Kentucky Revised Statute KRS Chapter 318 and 815 KAR 20:080, explaining the $250,000 GL minimum for master plumber licensing, the surety bond considerations for plumbing contractors, the specific water damage and completed operations exposure Kentucky plumbers face in the cold-weather months (freeze-thaw burst pipes along the Ohio River valley), and The Way Agency's real access to specialty carriers that restrict plumbing work will beat every generic national guide.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Kentucky plumbing contractors must carry at least $250,000 in general liability insurance to hold a master plumber or plumbing contractor license under 815 KAR 20:080. Most working contractors carry $1 million per occurrence to meet GC contract requirements. Workers compensation is also required for any employee under KRS 342.630. Completed operations and water damage liability are the two coverage gaps that cause the most denied claims.

entities_to_cover: Kentucky Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (DHBC)
815 KAR 20:080 (minimum insurance thresholds for plumbing contractors)
KRS Chapter 318 (plumbing permit and license statute)
general liability with water damage endorsement
master plumber license vs plumbing contractor license distinction
research_brief.local_angle: Kentucky plumbers face a freeze-thaw exposure unique to the Ohio River valley and Bullitt County climate, where burst pipe emergencies spike from November through February. New construction in Shepherdsville and Mt. Washington means more residential plumbing jobs on freshly built subdivisions, where a botched connection caught months later triggers a completed operations claim. The Way Agency knows which carriers will write plumbing in Kentucky without a plumbing exclusion, which is the most common coverage gap this agency sees in contractor policies written elsewhere.

candidates.title: Is the $25,000 Final Expense Benefit Real? What Kentucky Seniors Should Know
candidates.description: Explains the misleading $25,000 final expense ads targeting Kentucky seniors, what Social Security actually pays, and how legitimate burial insurance works.

research_brief.demand_evidence: GSC shows 6 variants of this query totaling 127+ impressions over 28 days at positions 4.2 to 10.1 with a combined 0 clicks, representing the agency's largest single content gap by impression volume. The '25k final expense package' variant alone sits at position 4.2 with 28 impressions and 0 CTR.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is occupied by Medium blog posts, a JustAnswer Q&A thread, a Substack piece, advocacy sites (voicesforsafety.com), and one insurance agent FAQ (thejordaninsuranceagency.com). No .gov source, no Kentucky-specific content, no independent agency with local authority. Content is thin, mostly 300-600 words, several pages more than a year old. No AI Overview was surfaced for the primary query variant tested, indicating the answer engine position is unclaimed.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: Every current page 1 result treats this as a national scam story. A post grounded in Kentucky reality - referencing the KY Attorney General's Office of Senior Protection, the 12-fold increase in KY scam reports since 2019, and the specific mailer and robocall tactics seniors in Bullitt and Daviess counties receive - out-competes on relevance. The post should also pivot constructively: yes, the $25,000 government benefit is a myth, but a legitimate $25,000 whole-life final expense policy IS available from real carriers, and here is what it actually costs and requires in Kentucky.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: There is no government program that pays a $25,000 final expense benefit to Kentucky seniors. Social Security pays a one-time $255 death benefit. Ads claiming otherwise are misleading marketing used to generate insurance leads. Legitimate final expense policies - small whole-life plans from licensed carriers - can provide $5,000 to $25,000 in real coverage, with premiums and eligibility that vary by age and health.

entities_to_cover: Kentucky Attorney General Office of Senior Protection
FTC consumer alerts on senior fraud
KY DOI licensed carrier lookup at insurance.ky.gov
guaranteed-issue vs simplified-issue final expense policies
research_brief.local_angle: Kentucky saw a 12-fold increase in scam reports between 2019 and the pandemic years, with the KY Attorney General's Office of Senior Protection receiving over 7,000 scam reports in 2021 alone. Seniors in Bullitt and Daviess counties are receiving these mailers and robocalls. A licensed KY independent agent can verify any carrier through insurance.ky.gov and shop A-rated carriers - something no mailer or robocall can offer.

Key local considerations include hail and wind exposure from Ohio Valley storms, I-65 commuter accident rates, and the newer construction profile of Shepherdsville subdivisions, which affects replacement cost calculations. candidates.title: Why Your Insurance Premium Changed at Renewal: A Kentucky Policyholder's Guide
candidates.description: Explains the Kentucky-specific rules governing policy renewals, why premiums rise even without claims, and what policyholders can do when their renewal notice arrives.
secondary_keywords: why did my insurance premium go up at renewal

research_brief.demand_evidence: The query 'insurance renewal process' holds position 19 with 40 impressions and only 1 click in the 28-day window - the second-highest impression count among non-brand queries after the final expense cluster. Position 19 with this volume means a dedicated post targeting the consumer (not agent-licensing) angle can realistically move to page 1. The published 'understanding-your-policy-renewal-process' covers the agency operations side; this post targets the policyholder asking why their premium changed.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is occupied by B2B/insurer-side content (selectsys.com insurance software, exdioninsurance.com agency operations), generic consumer explainers (trustmypolicy.com, insurancecurator.com, bpo.click-vision.com), and one home insurance-specific piece (pennypincher.com). No Kentucky-specific page exists anywhere in the top 20. The Kentucky DOI has a direct-authority .gov PDF on non-renewal of personal auto policies (howcantheydothat071217.pdf) that no local agency is citing or interpreting for consumers.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: Differentiation is KY statutory specificity. The KY DOI PDF establishes that for personal auto non-renewals, the insurer must send written notice at least 30 days before the end of the current policy period. Kentucky also does not prohibit credit scoring in underwriting or rating - a fact that surprises many policyholders who assume a claim-free record protects them from premium increases. Anchoring these statutory facts makes the post the authoritative KY consumer answer while every competitor publishes generic content.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: In Kentucky, insurance companies must send a renewal notice at least 30 days before your policy ends for personal auto coverage. Your premium can change at renewal for reasons unrelated to your claims - including credit score changes, local weather loss trends, construction costs, or reinsurance market shifts. Reviewing the renewal notice carefully and asking an independent agent to re-shop the market is the single most effective action you can take.
questions_to_answer: Why did my home insurance go up at renewal even though I filed no claims?
How much notice does my insurance company have to give before not renewing in Kentucky?

Does my credit score affect my renewal premium in Kentucky?
research_brief.local_angle: Kentucky does not prohibit the use of credit scores in insurance rating, meaning a dip in credit - even with no claims - can trigger a premium increase at renewal. Bullitt County and Daviess County homeowners have also seen above-average rate increases due to hail claim frequency along the Ohio Valley corridor. An independent agent at The Way Agency can re-shop across multiple carriers during the renewal window at no cost to the policyholder.

candidates.title: Professional Liability Insurance in Kentucky: Who Needs E&O and What It Costs
candidates.description: A plain-language Kentucky guide to professional liability (E&O) insurance - who needs it, what KY law requires, what it costs, and how it differs from general liability.
secondary_keywords: do I need professional liability insurance Kentucky
professional liability vs general liability Kentucky

research_brief.demand_evidence: The agency product page /commercial/professional-liability.html exists with no supporting blog content. The 'insurance types coverage comparing quotes claims' query (position 1.5, 83.3% CTR) signals strong demand for coverage comparison content, and E&O vs GL is the most common comparison question from commercial prospects. The query 'professional liability insurance Kentucky' has consistent SERP activity with no local Kentucky agency holding a top-10 editorial position.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is occupied by biberk.com, techinsurance.com, insureon.com, bizinsure.com, allenthomasgroup.com, and progressivecommercial.com. The one KY-local result is ekinsurance.com (Winchester, KY) with a thin 400-word page. No result addresses the Kentucky-specific mandatory E&O requirement for real estate agents (KRS 324), the $20,000 surety bond requirement for Kentucky insurance consultants (KRS 304.9-105 and 304.9-330), or the lack of a general state mandate for other professions. The average cost data available ($88/month) comes from TechInsurance national averages with no KY-specific context.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: Anchor the post in KY statutory specificity: real estate agents and brokers in Kentucky are required by state law (KRS 324) to carry E&O. Insurance consultants must carry a $20,000 surety bond under KRS 304.9-105. For all other professions, professional liability is not legally mandated in Kentucky - but contract requirements and client demands often make it a practical requirement. The post should also explain the GL gap: general liability covers bodily injury and property damage, not financial harm from professional advice. A Kentucky consultant who gives bad advice that costs a client $50,000 has zero GL protection.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Professional liability insurance (also called E&O or errors and omissions insurance) protects Kentucky businesses when a client claims your advice, service, or failure to act caused them financial harm. General liability will not cover this - it only covers physical injury and property damage. Kentucky real estate agents are required by state law to carry E&O. For most other professions, it is not legally required but is often demanded by contracts and clients.
questions_to_answer: What is professional liability insurance and how is it different from general liability in Kentucky?
Does Kentucky require professional liability insurance?
Who needs errors and omissions insurance in Kentucky?
How much does professional liability insurance cost for a Kentucky small business?
Does a Kentucky real estate agent have to carry E&O insurance?
What does professional liability insurance NOT cover?
Can a Kentucky consultant be sued even if they did nothing wrong?
research_brief.local_angle: Owensboro's growing downtown professional services sector - accountants, consultants, architects, healthcare administrators - and Bullitt County's expanding contractor and engineering population both generate demand for E&O coverage. The Way Agency serves both markets and can place professional liability for industries ranging from home inspectors to IT consultants to non-profit administrators, which most storefront captive agents cannot access.
